project_name: Holder Industrial Park data center rezoning
aliases: Deltona Corporation Holder Industrial Park proposal
status_detail: Planning and Development Commission rejected land-use/zoning changes on June 18, 2026; Deltona then withdrew applications CPA-2-2025-000012 and CPA 2025-000013 concerning Holder Industrial Park after county commissioners denied a delay request.
notes: Proposal sought to convert roughly 798 additional acres near North Lecanto Highway/North Tram Road/North Florida Avenue and combine with the existing ~557-acre Holder Industrial Park, for roughly 1,300-1,400 acres that could allow a data center. Included despite withdrawal because county process reached public review.

status_detail: No specific Clay County FL data center developer, site plan, rezoning, permit, or tax-abatement project found. County commissioners approved a one-year moratorium on data center facilities on June 23/24, 2026, pausing rezoning, permits, and site plans while staff studies impacts.
notes: Search hits were moratorium/regulatory coverage and generic vendor landing pages; no named local project located.

status_detail: No confirmed Collier County FL data center project/application found. Reporting says commissioners continued a zoning-in-progress approach while drafting rules for possible future hyperscale/AI data centers.
notes: Official zoning/permit pages reviewed for process context; available evidence points to preemptive regulation, not a named facility.

status_detail: No Columbia County, Florida data center project/application found on county zoning pages or targeted searches. Many prominent 'Columbia County data center' results refer to Columbia County, Georgia, not Florida.
notes: Checked county official website, zoning/permit resources, and web/news queries for data center/server farm/hyperscale/colocation; no Florida county project located.

aliases: DeSoto County Industrial Park data center
developer: DCIP / DeSoto County Industrial Park LLC
status_detail: DeSoto County official data-center applications page says DCIP received Board approval on March 24, 2026 for PUD rezoning and a concept development plan for a 35,134-square-foot data center facility and office with an electrical generation facility at 3800 NE Roan Road.
notes: Initial phase on 34.22 acres at a decommissioned power plant/industrial park site; county page labels the development as a hyperscale data center.

status_detail: Official DeSoto County page lists a PUD rezoning/hyperscale data center application received May 7, 2026 for 274.26 acres and a 3,686,125-square-foot hyperscale data center; concept plan groups it with the DCIP master data center facility.
notes: County page says both newer applications require Planning Commission and Board public hearings; status treated as planned/application pending rather than approved.

aliases: Swisher Mildred E TR data center
developer: Swisher Mildred E TR & Swisher Properties
status_detail: Official DeSoto County page lists a PUD rezoning/hyperscale data center application received May 13, 2026 for 553.79 acres and a 4,655,000-square-foot hyperscale data center with electrical generation facility.
notes: Together with DCIP/3-F Ranch, the county concept plan shows ~825.97 total project acres and ~8.37 million square feet of proposed building area; application pending hearings in this pass.

status_detail: No named Dixie County FL data center project/application found. County clerk posted a July 24, 2026 BOCC workshop notice regarding an AI/Data Center moratorium request, but no developer, parcel, permit, or rezoning record was identified.
notes: Local/social discussion exists around a data-center workshop; included as coverage evidence only, not as project evidence.

status_detail: Cologix official Jacksonville page lists JAX1 at 421 West Church Street as a Jacksonville data center/interconnect hub; Cleanview/datacentermap identify it as operating in Duval County, with year operational 2013 in Cleanview.
notes: No MW found on operator page; third-party tracker gives facility metadata but no capacity for JAX1.

status_detail: Cologix official Jacksonville page lists JAX2 at 4800 Spring Park Road as an enterprise-grade Jacksonville data center and disaster recovery facility; Cleanview lists it as operating, 1 MW, year operational 2014, in Duval County.
notes: Capacity from tracker; operator confirms address and operating facility identity.

status_detail: TierPoint official page lists a Jacksonville data center at 8324 Baymeadows Way with 120,000+ total square feet, 17,000+ square feet raised floor, two 2 MW redundant generators, colocation/managed services, and compliance certifications; Cleanview lists 4 MW operating capacity in Duval County.
notes: Capacity taken from Cleanview because TierPoint page specifies generator configuration rather than sellable/load capacity.

status_detail: Flexential search-indexed operator page lists its Jacksonville colocation data center at 4905 Belfort Road, Suite 145, with 35,184 square feet of data center footprint and 1.39 MW.
notes: Operator page timed out when opened in full but search snippet exposed address, footprint, and MW; Baxtel/DatacenterMap corroborate Jacksonville market/facility presence.

status_detail: Cleanview lists EdgeConneX JAX01 as an operating Duval County data center with 1 MW capacity and 17,570 square feet.
notes: Included for super-set coverage from trackers; operator page was not located quickly in this pass.

status_detail: No confirmed Escambia County FL project found. May 2026 TV report said one unnamed company was in active negotiations for a smaller facility, but FloridaWest CEO Chris Plate later told commissioners there were no active negotiations, no proposal, no incentive commitment, and no pending public action; commissioners then approved an ordinance blocking large-scale data centers in unincorporated areas on August 6/7, 2026.
notes: Tracked as no_projects_found because the EDA denial and lack of public action outweigh the earlier unnamed negotiation report.

project_name: DC BLOX Palm Coast data center and Google Sol cable landing station
aliases: DC BLOX Flagler County data center
status_detail: Flagler County official news release says DC BLOX will build a high-capacity next-generation data center on 34 acres within Town Center, designed for up to six subsea cable landings, launching with Google’s Sol Cable Landing Station connecting Palm Coast to Bermuda, the Azores, and Spain.
notes: Later county moratorium applies to unincorporated Flagler County and Observer reporting says it does not affect municipal projects; county chair distinguished Palm Coast's DC BLOX project from county approvals.
